title: The reading is the job
eyebrow: Two faults you pointed out have one cause: being read is a piece of work rather than something that happens to a job.

actions.fyi: Nothing is waiting on you. Override any decision below if you disagree with one.

content.label: What is wrong
content.lead: Being read is currently a task on the job's own list, and that single fact causes both things you saw.

rows.title: Agent Review can never mean what it says
rows.note: A job is moved into that column at the moment its reading task opens — and that task is one of its own pieces. So the column's rule, every piece closed, is false the instant it is written. Three jobs sit like that right now.

rows.title: Work done in answer to a reader is never read
rows.note: The reader signs the task once. Nothing ties that signature to what it was signing, so the same session can answer the objections, write new work, and tick the task off on the old signature.

rows.title: The check meant to stop self-review cannot fire
rows.note: It compares the signature against the names on the job's other tasks. The session doing the closing is not on that list and is not the signature, so it is never the thing being tested.

content.label: Watched happening first
content.lead: All three checked against the live board before anything was designed.

rows: Agent Review always holds an open piece
3 jobs in the column, 3 with exactly one open piece, and in every case it is the reading itself
One signature covers two rounds of work
5 changes belong to that job; 3 of them were written after it was signed, and nobody read those
The self-review check cannot fire
it compares the signature against one name, and the session doing the closing is not that name

content.label: What changes
content.lead: The reading stops being a piece of work and becomes a state the job is in, the way being in progress already is.

rows: A job in Agent Review
always has one open piece
has none — that is what puts it there
The signature
never expires
names the work it read, and goes stale when new work lands
Answering a reader
closes on the old signature
sends the job back to be read again, by itself
Who may sign
anyone not on a task list
nobody who touched the job, the closing session included
A job nobody read
can reach done
cannot leave the column at all

blocks.label: Nothing is lost
blocks.text: The reader is still fetched by the board, still refused the edit tools, and what it finds still becomes the job's own work. Only where the signature lives changes.

blocks.label: Checked before designing on it
blocks.text: A job has to sit in the column and be held shut at the same time. Read off a job that is held shut today: being held does not overwrite where a card is drawn, so both are possible at once.

content.label: How we know it works
content.lead: Four cases in the board's own suite, each one a way the old behaviour could come back.

rows: A job with nothing left to build and no signature
The same job after it answered its reader
A job read already, with nothing written since
A job whose only signature is from a hand that wrote it

blocks.label: Why the second row is the whole point
blocks.text: That is the case that let a job answer its reader and finish on the reading that had turned it down. It is now the same test as the first row, not a special path.

content.label: The old cards are gone
content.lead: Every reading card that existed has been retired, and nothing can make another.

rows: Reading cards on the board before
Reading cards on the board now
Jobs freed to be read, held shut until they are

blocks.label: Confirmed by running it, not by reading it
blocks.text: Every one of the twelve positions a job can run was offered to the thing that makes cards. Ten make one; the work and the reading make none. Putting the reading back on the list makes the check fail.

blocks.label: Found while doing it
blocks.text: The board answers "nothing" in a way that is not an empty list, and three places took that as a broken answer and crashed. Fixed, and it is the reason to run a change against the real board and not only against a stand-in.

decisions.title: The column stays, the task goes
decisions.why: Your ruling. The two could not both be true, and the column is the half a reader of the board actually uses.

decisions.title: The signature records what it read
decisions.why: An expiry rule needs something to expire against. Recording the work read at signing time is what lets the board tell an answered objection from an unread one, without asking anybody.

decisions.title: Three jobs already stuck are freed by this, not migrated by hand
decisions.why: Each is read where it stands the first time anything moves on it. A hand migration would be a script that exists to be deleted.

decisions.title: A signature goes stale at one point only
decisions.why: If it went stale against every later change, the write-it-down step that comes after the reading would make every job permanently unread and nothing could ever finish. It is asked where the board decides whether to read again, and nowhere else.

next.if_nothing: The three stuck jobs start moving again and every job from here on is read before it can finish.

steps.step: The three jobs stuck in Agent Review get read and start closing
